## Some Important Sports Cups and Trophies
### Stanley Cup
The Stanley Cup, given yearly to the National Hockey League (NHL) champion, is the oldest professional sports trophy in North America. The Tampa Bay Lightning is the current holder.

### UEFA Champions League Trophy
The annual club football competition, put on by the Union of European Football Associations, is known as the UEFA Champions League Trophy (UEFA). Chelsea is the reigning champion.

### America’s Cup
America’s Cup is the oldest sporting trophy in the world and is given to the victor of America’s Cup yacht race. New Zealand is the holder at the moment.

## **What Is the Oldest Sports Trophy in the World?**
The title of the oldest sporting trophy in the world is widely attributed to the America’s Cup, first awarded in 1851. Originally known as the “Hundred Guinea Cup,” it was presented after a yacht race around the Isle of Wight in England.

## **10 Oldest Sports Trophies Still Awarded Today**
### **10. Stanley Cup – 1893, Canada**
The Stanley Cup is the oldest professional sports trophy in North America and is awarded annually to the champions of the National Hockey League. Named after Lord Stanley of Preston, the Governor General of Canada in 1892, the trophy has a unique feature. Unlike most awards, it is not recreated each year.

# Five things you didn’t know about the Stanley Cup, ice hockey’s most iconic trophy
At 35.25 inches tall and weighing 34.5 pounds, “The Cup” is no ordinary prize. Lovingly dubbed “The Holy Grail” or “Lord Stanley’s Mug,” it’s the oldest **contested trophy in North American sports** , and without a doubt the most well-travelled.
After its annual victory lap with the newly crowned NHL champions, it earns up to 100,000 miles a year, raising charity dollars, turning up at weddings, parades, and lakeside parties, and stealing the spotlight at every turn.

...

## **1. The Stanley Cup is the oldest sports trophy in North America**
Before it was hoisted by NHL legends or carted around in convertibles, the Stanley Cup was a silver rose bowl, purchased from a London jeweller by a British lord with a growing fondness for Canada’s icy obsession.
Back in 1892, **Lord Frederick Stanley of Preston** , then Canada’s Governor General, fell in love with hockey after watching a match at Montreal’s Winter Carnival. Moved by the passion and potential of the fledgling sport, he decided it deserved a proper prize.

...

Over time, the Cup evolved in tandem with the game itself. By 1910, it symbolized professional hockey supremacy, and from 1926 onwards, it became the exclusive prize of NHL champions.
That humble rose bowl is now an icon in itself, with more than **3,300 names engraved on its gleaming surface** , and a history that predates every NHL franchise still skating today.

...

## **3. Every winner’s name is engraved on the Stanley Cup**
In its early days, a new band was added every year to accommodate the latest champions, resulting in a tall, towering structure that eventually became impractical, earning it the nickname “ **the stovepipe** .” In 1948, a redesign gave the trophy its modern silhouette, and by 1958,

...

## **“The Stanley Cup is meant to be shared and enjoyed"**
To this day, it doesn’t sit quietly in a case; it lives a full, unruly, and unforgettable life. With the 2025 champions soon to be crowned, the ice hockey world holds its breath to see what the Cup will be up to next.

# 10 Oldest Sports Trophies in the World
## 10. Stanley Cup
**Year Created:** 1892
**First Year Awarded:** 1893
**Sport:** Hockey
**Country of Origin:** Canada
Stanley Cup photo source: [Wikimedia Commons via Alex Goykhman](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Stanley_Cup,_2015.jpg)
Although the [Stanley Cup](https://www.hhof.com/htmlSilverware/silver_splashstanleycup.shtml) may not be as old as some of the other trophies on the list, it is the oldest professional sports trophy in North America.
The Stanley Cup was donated by and named for Sir Frederick Arthur Stanley, Lord Stanley of Preston and son of the 14th Earl of Derby. Lord Stanley paid about 10 Guineas ($50.00 at that time) for the trophy, which he wanted to present to “the champion hockey team in the Dominion of Canada.”
The Stanley Cup was awarded for the first time in 1893 to the Montreal Amateur Athletic Association. In its early years, the Stanley Cup was given to the winners of challenge games involving the top amateur teams in Canada.

excerpts:
# The Stanley Cup National Historic Event
Importance: One of the oldest and most prestigious trophies to be won by professional athletes in North America

## Plaque(s)
**Approved Inscription:**
Brimming with dreams of championship glory, the Stanley Cup is the oldest and most prestigious trophy in North American team sports. In 1892, Governor General Lord Stanley’s donation of a challenge cup for Canada’s best hockey club was announced near here.
First awarded to amateur teams, the Stanley Cup has been the exclusive prize of the National Hockey League’s playoff champion since 1927. Many legends of the game have hoisted the Cup, their names engraved on its silver.

results.title: The Stanley Cup Trophy
excerpts:
# The Stanley Cup Trophy
The **Stanley Cup** is a championship trophy awarded yearly to the National Hockey League (NHL) playoff winners.
The Stanley Cup The Stanley Cup
The Stanley Cup is North America's oldest professional sports trophy. The trophy is named after Lord Stanley of Preston, the Governor General of Canada who donated it as an award to Canada's top-ranking amateur ice hockey club.
There are three versions of the "Stanley Cup": the original 1892 bowl or Dominion Hockey Challenge Cup, the 1963 authenticated "Presentation Cup", and the 1993 "Permanent Cup" at the Hall of Fame.
The Stanley Cup is engraved with the names of the winning players, coaches, management, and club staff.
